newsitem.title: USA: S&P says credit improved in north central region.
newsitem.headline: S&P says credit improved in north central region.

text.p: Municipal credit ratings in the north central region generally improved last year mirroring a national trend, Standard & Poor's Corp. said Monday in its CreditWeek Municipal publication.

The rating agency said upgrades exceeded downgrades by a 4 to 1 ratio in the region composed of Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Wisconsin, Ohio, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, North Dakota, South Dakota and Nebraska.

In the tax-backed sector, Standard & Poor's noted the upgrade of Ohio's general obligation rating to AA-plus from AA. The rating agency also pointed out that Detroit and Indianapolis also face possible upgrades as the agency mantains a positive outlook on their ratings.
The rating agency said the region still faces challenges such as the volatility of the manufacturing sector.

Standard & Poor's said the governments must be positioned for the potential of an economic slowdown, while addressing capital needs. In addition, the governments need to maintain and attract sufficient labor forces and improve economic diversity, the rating agency said.
